newsitem.title: USA: Auditor says solid Miami numbers due by Jan 1.
newsitem.headline: Auditor says solid Miami numbers due by Jan 1.

text.p: Miami's new external auditor said Thursday that he expects to have the city's annual report for fiscal 1996 completed by March 31.
The report by KPMG Peat Marwick should provide an accurate statement of the city's bottom line, Peat Marwick accountant Jose Rodriguez told the city commission.
City officials have estimated Miami's deficit at $68 million for the year that began Oct 1, but they acknowledged that estimate is based on a budget that was "largely fiction."
Rodriguez also urged the comission to act "on a post-haste basis" to beef up staffing and expertise levels in its finance department.
"You are between 20 and 45 days behind on your postings, and you're also behind on bank reconciliations," Rodriguez told commissioners.
City Manager Ed Marquez said would interview candidates for city finance director over the next two or three weeks and hoped to have a director on staff in early January.
He said the city hoped to have its accounts up to date by the end of December.
The city's former finance director, Manohar Surana, resigned on August 30 to face federal corruption charges.
